recheck.why:
Lint is clean (1.000, 0 errors, 0 advisories) and the pack consistency checker returns nothing for this slug. Role/level are exactly applications-engineer/fresher. All ten declared slots are spent. The record block correctly avoids the held noun "boundary" (verified: dv-ams-view-binding-audit, dv-connect-module-discipline-debug and dv-asset-flow-property-authoring all carry a bare `boundary` field) and puts `notes` last per the vocabulary. The domain judgement is largely excellent. But two of the review's own questions fail, so I would not hand this to an AE today.

BLOCKER 1 - the budget does not account for every Grep. The re-sweep of the redacted copy is mandatory in three places: step 6 ("a redaction nobody re-swept is a redaction nobody verified" - and the only reason the agent is given the copy's path), step 7 ("egress: redact-then-release - the map exists, it has been applied to a copy, and the re-sweep of that copy is clean"), and Done when ("the copy has been re-swept clean"). Budget rule 3 allocates exactly "one for provenance in step 2, eight class sweeps in step 4, and one spare... There is no second spare" - so 0 to 1 Greps remain when the copy arrives, against the up-to-8 a re-sweep needs. Worse, budget rule 6's stopping rule ("Stop when all ten classes have a verdict or the budget is spent") positively forbids it. The most common non-hold verdict in the skill cannot be reached inside the skill's own caps. Fix: either budget a second pass explicitly, or say the re-sweep is a fresh invocation of this procedure on the copy's path.

BLOCKER 2 - class 8 Greps for something the engineer was never asked to define. Class 8 "Tool internals" sources its pattern from Restricted vocabulary, whose slot reads "[[FILL: the project codenames, unreleased part names and internal feature-flag strings that must never leave...]]". That slot contains nothing about "our own build's file paths and flag names", and by the skill's own prose those paths belong to Path roots ("Path roots is the set of roots appearing inside logs, a larger set including tool, release and home areas") i.e. class 2. Class 4 already consumes the entire Restricted vocabulary slot verbatim ("codenames, unreleased part names, feature-flag strings"). So line 143-144's claim that "class 8 [spends] the tool half of Restricted vocabulary - shared slots, separate patterns, separate hit counts" is not true of the slot as written: unlike Identity patterns, which genuinely spans machines and people in its own FILL text and gets an explanatory paragraph naming both owners, Restricted vocabulary has no tool half. In practice the agent either invents a pattern for tool-internal paths (standing rules 2 and 4) or re-runs class 4's pattern and reports a duplicate hit count as a separate class.

Everything else checked: no proprietary flags, message strings or house conventions asserted outside slots; pasted-text case handled in step 1 as required; coverage line and residual are honest; frontmatter keys exactly the required set; review-by 2027-05-12 is unique in the pack and ~9 months out.
remaining: BLOCKER: the mandatory re-sweep of the redacted copy (step 6, step 7 redact-then-release, Done when) has no Grep allocation - budget rule 3 caps at 10 Greps (1 provenance + 8 classes + 1 spare, 'no second spare') and budget rule 6's stopping rule forbids continuing. Allocate a second pass, or state that the re-sweep is a fresh invocation of the procedure on the copy's path.

BLOCKER: class 8 'Tool internals' cites Restricted vocabulary as its pattern source, but that slot only asks for codenames, unreleased part names and feature-flag strings - class 4 already consumes it whole. 'Our own build's file paths' is Path roots by the skill's own prose. Either widen the Restricted vocabulary slot text to name the tool half (as Identity patterns does for its people half, with the matching 'ask both owners' paragraph), or fold class 8's paths into class 2 and free the Grep.

Line 32: 'dv-sim-log-first-error emits a repro block whose log and run id fields are a path and a machine identity' - wrong about run id. Its block reads 'run id : <whatever identifies this run for us>', and _shared/handoff-vocabulary.md T3 defines run id as the profile's Run identity fact, which is 'seed, test name, configuration, build tag' - not a machine identity. The field in that block that actually carries farm/licence layout is 'to repeat'. This is the 'two differently-named facts are the same fact' error the standing rules call out.

The record block offers 'unswept : <files and formats no search could reach, named>' but no numbered step assigns it - step 1 records paths and artifact kind, step 4 sweeps ten classes, and only a Gotcha bullet ('Binary and derived artifacts cannot be swept... They belong under unswept') names it. Give step 1 the job of marking unsweepable members while it is already listing the package.

Class 5 'Credential-shaped' makes 'hold, and rotation by its owner' the disposition for every hit, including licence checkout lines - a licence checkout line has no secret to rotate, and licence server entries are already class 1 with the conflicting disposition 'replace with a stable placeholder'. Say which half of a licence line is class 1 and which (if any) is class 5, or drop licence lines from class 5.

Step 6's example map row '<work-root> location 212' sits right against budget rule 5 ('more than about 200 hits... spend the spare and narrow it once... still that broad, the class is pervasive: step 7 turns it into egress: hold'). Occurrences and Grep line-hits are not the same count, but nothing says so, and the illustrative map reads as an ordinary redact-then-release case for a number the budget treats as pervasive.

The step 6 fenced map uses the bare column header 'class' with values 'machine identity', 'location', 'attribution'. 'class' is the pack's most-shared registered enum (design | infrastructure | unknown, 44 skills, narrowing 'no'). The consistency checker does not see it because the block is whitespace-aligned rather than 'name : value', so this is style not a mechanical failure - but the skill takes care to avoid 'boundary' for exactly this reason and should apply the same care here ('redaction class' costs one word).
271 lines against the stated 180-260 ceiling. Non-blocking in practice - published siblings run 260 to 456 - but worth knowing it is over.
